p: Parents of teenagers will know the struggle. The summer holidays drag on, the screens have been glued to hands for days, and you need something that gets them out and actually excited. Karting is a winner because it's fast, it's competitive and it feels grown up without being out of reach.
Plan ahead, though. School holidays are peak time, and slots go quickly. Check the junior age and height rules before you book, and make sure everyone has suitable shoes and clothes on the day.
If you're bringing a group of their friends, it's worth having a simple plan for afterwards, whether it's food or a park, because a bunch of teenagers fresh out of a kart will be buzzing.
One last parent tip: take a few photos of them in their helmets before the race. They'll pretend to hate it, but those pictures always end up as the profile picture by the end of the week.

Edmonton puts you close to some great spots. The Lee Valley Regional Park stretches along this side of London, with walking and cycling routes along the river and reservoirs. Football fans have the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium a short hop away, which offers stadium tours on non-match days. Getting around is easy too, with trains and buses connecting the area to central London.
